WHAT THE OVERRIDE RATE COUNTS decisions that went against the advice ÷ decisions that had advice 0 ÷ 0 = — 0 of the 0 decisions shown had no recommendation at the time, so they are left out. 3 Demo Mode rows are shown on the board with a demo label and counted in none of the numbers above HR-01 / THE HUMAN GATE ADVISORY ONLY Scores are advice. People decide. Scores are advisory. No candidate may be rejected without a named human and a written reason; the database enforces this. That sentence is shown again beside the score history when you open a candidate, and every row on the board is captioned “advisory — a human decides”. Nothing here turns anyone down on its own A rejection needs a named person and a reason written out. Without both, the system refuses to record it. No score closes an application, and there is no list of canned reasons to pick from. Recommendations are all one colour on purpose. A red-amber-green light would turn advice into a verdict, which is the one thing this screen must not do. HR-02 / THE BENCH ALWAYS-ON RECRUITING WORST SHORTFALL FIRST ROLE BENCH (1:1 + offer, open) SHORTFALL OPEN APPLICATIONS AWAITING SCREEN AWAITING GROUP INTERVIEW HIRING MANAGER FLAGS Closer 0 / 4 target for this role 4 0 0 not screened yet 0 at group interview unassigned SHORT UNROUTED Sales Coordinator 0 / 4 target for this role 4 0 0 not screened yet 0 at group interview unassigned SHORT UNROUTED Setter 0 / 4 target for this role 4 0 0 not screened yet 0 at group interview unassigned SHORT UNROUTED The bench is open applications sitting at 1:1 Interview or Offer. Nothing earlier counts, so a stack of unscreened applications can never read as a healthy bench. Shortfall is the target minus the bench, and never goes below zero. The target is 4 people per role unless it was changed for that role. Unrouted means the role has no hiring manager — nobody owns it. Nothing checks the bench on a schedule yet, so there is no “last checked” time to show. The board is not draggable — nothing on this screen can move a candidate from one stage to another. Stage and status are two different things, and they can disagree. The stage filter filters the stage. There is no way to filter on status. The Hired stage is a trap. A candidate who is moved into Hired is frozen there and cannot be moved again. Onboarding, Ramp and Performing can only be reached by skipping straight past Hired, which leaves the status showing open. So neither column is a count of the people working here — do not read it as one. The score block always travels together — average, recommendation, rubric version and flag count in one place, captioned as advice. The card shows the latest score only; the full history is on the candidate, so there is no trend line to draw here. The card knows only whether a video and a resume exist. Open the candidate to watch the video; the resume itself cannot be opened from anywhere on this screen. showing 3 of 3 loaded applications · 3 of them seeded by Demo Mode, labelled on the card and counted nowhere · up to 200 are loaded at a time, and no screen-wide total is available HR-04 / NEEDS A HUMAN 0 WAITING · 0 OPEN · 3 DEMO NOT COUNTED FLAGGED OR NOT SCORED CANDIDATE ROLE STAGE STATUS AVERAGE RECOMMENDATION RUBRIC WHY IT IS HERE IN STAGE DEMO Candidate — Juniper Vale DEMO ROW 291d880e-eb62-47ef-b1c5-8b6c85d0fc84 · inbound Closer Applied OPEN not scored no score advisory — a human decides no rubric Not scored No reason for the missing score was recorded. -6d since Aug 05 DEMO Candidate — Cedar Holt DEMO ROW 519e846b-8765-47af-b1bf-8c167b69f7fd · inbound Closer Screening OPEN not scored no score advisory — a human decides no rubric Not scored No reason for the missing score was recorded. -6d since Aug 05 DEMO Candidate — Maple Crest DEMO ROW 688467d4-7490-4075-991c-acf54d3a2bb1 · inbound Closer Group Interview OPEN not scored no score advisory — a human decides no rubric Not scored No reason for the missing score was recorded. -6d since Aug 05 A candidate lands here for one of two reasons: the grader flagged something, or it could not produce a score at all. A missing score is shown as not scored, never as a low score. The moment one part of the scorecard is left blank, the whole score is withheld — averaging the three answers somebody happened to fill in is how a good candidate gets marked “below bar” off one question. Closed applications keep showing up here until someone scores them again. They are dimmed rather than hidden, because hiding them would make this queue look shorter than it is. Nothing here is waiting on a scorecard rule the grader cannot check. Every row is here because it was flagged by a check that ran, or because it has no score at all.
